title: Undoing Things Safely: revert, reset, and reflog
intro: Git has several ways to undo, and choosing the wrong one on a shared branch turns a small mistake into a team-wide problem. Here's which one to use when.

steps.prompt: Commit b7c8d9e on main broke production. Undo it in a way that's safe on a shared branch.
steps.fake_output:
[main 3e4f5a6] Revert "feat: new pricing engine"
 3 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 41 deletions(-)
steps.explanation: A NEW commit that undoes b7c8d9e's changes. History is preserved; nothing is rewritten.
steps.why: revert is the right tool for anything already pushed: everyone's history stays consistent, the CI pipeline deploys it like any other commit, and there's a clear record of what was undone and why.

steps.prompt: On your local-only experiment branch, throw away the last 2 commits entirely.
steps.fake_output: HEAD is now at a1b2c3d release v2.3.0
steps.explanation: The branch pointer moves back 2 commits and the working directory matches — those commits (and any uncommitted changes) are gone from the branch.
steps.why: reset --hard rewrites history and discards uncommitted work. Fine on a private branch; on main, it breaks everyone who already pulled. Rule of thumb: pushed = revert, not pushed = reset is okay.

steps.prompt: Oops — one of those 2 commits was actually needed. Find it in the reflog.
steps.fake_output:
a1b2c3d HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~2
e4f5a6b HEAD@{1}: commit: add discount codes
c3d4e5f HEAD@{2}: commit: fix cart total rounding
steps.explanation: The reflog records every position HEAD has been at — including commits no branch points to anymore.
steps.why: This is git's safety net: 'deleted' commits aren't really gone for ~90 days. Knowing reflog exists turns a panic moment into a 30-second recovery.

steps.prompt: Restore the needed commit e4f5a6b onto your branch.
steps.fake_output:
[experiment 5b6c7d8] add discount codes
 2 files changed, 30 insertions(+)
steps.why: cherry-pick brings back just that one commit; 'git reset --hard e4f5a6b' moves the branch back to that point entirely. Choose based on whether you want one commit or the whole previous state.
